Choice, buying, pricing and availability words tend negative; outdoor,
email, pets, children and selected household/device nouns tend positive.

Dotted find/get tokens have a small positive baseline.

    'popular', 'top', 'informed', 'standout', 'finest',
}

}

            value -= 0.150
        elif any(w in EVALUATIONS for w in recent):
            value -= 0.068
        if group in {'choice', 'choose', 'buy', 'decision'} and before in MODALS:
            value -= 0.038

Punctuation, case, and whether bare 'go' continues a word affect its strength.
The previous token is used only within the same document, including to join
'g' + 'olang'. All other spellings are assigned zero. This deliberately omits
weak, idiosyncratic responses to unrelated tokens and most context variation.
"""

"""Component layers.0.mlp.down_proj:3906 is a "go" detector.

It fires on the verb "go" and its forms, most strongly on "go" written as a
standalone word or name: " go", "Go", "GO", and "go" after a dot, slash or
dash, as in Go-language code (".go" files, "github.com/x/y-go", "/go").
Weaker, by a roughly fixed amount, it fires on the other forms of the verb
(going, went, goes, gone), on "goto" and "golang", on the same meaning in
other languages (đi, ไป, 去), and more faintly on motion and light verbs
(come, travel, proceed, do, take, keep, put, move). A bare "go" glued to the
end of a word fragment (as in Polish or Hungarian text) stays low. Everything
else predicts 0.

Stateless: each position is judged from its own token and, for one case,
the token before it.
"""

import re

READS = ()

GO_STANDALONE = 6.0      # " go", " Go", "GO", ".go", "/go", "-go"
GO_FRAGMENT = 2.4        # "go" glued to a word fragment, no punctuation or space
GO_FORMS = {"going": 3.7, "went": 3.7, "goes": 4.1, "gone": 3.0,
            "goto": 2.1, "olang": 2.9}  # "olang": the tail of ".golang"
GO_OTHER = {"đi": 2.9, "ไป": 3.5, "去": 1.7}
MOTION = {"come": 1.4, "came": 1.1, "comes": 1.2, "coming": 0.7, "travel": 1.1,
          "travelling": 1.1, "traveling": 1.2, "proceed": 1.7, "proceeds": 1.2,
          "proceeding": 1.2, "走": 1.5, "来": 0.8}
LIGHT_VERBS = {"do": 0.6, "does": 0.6, "did": 0.5, "done": 0.7, "take": 0.6,
               "takes": 0.5, "took": 0.5, "taken": 0.6, "keep": 0.9, "kept": 0.7,
               "put": 0.7, "move": 0.8, "moving": 0.7}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    core = re.sub(r"[^\w一-鿿]", "", word).lower()
    if core == "go":
        if word == core:
            # bare "go": a word of its own after a space-less boundary is
            # "go"; one glued to a preceding letter is a word fragment
            before = prefix.token_strings[-2] if len(prefix) > 1 else ""
            fragment = before[-1:].isalpha()
            return carry, GO_FRAGMENT if fragment else GO_STANDALONE
        return carry, GO_STANDALONE
    for table in (GO_FORMS, GO_OTHER, MOTION, LIGHT_VERBS):
        if core in table:
            return carry, table[core]
    if word.strip().lower() in GO_OTHER:
        return carry, GO_OTHER[word.strip().lower()]
    return carry, 0.0

"""A partial explanation: language-sensitive dashes and conversation boundaries.

Count completed function words and accented words over the last 96 tokens.
Romance-language evidence raises dash responses; English, competing Latin-script
languages and code symbols reduce that evidence. Cyrillic words give a smaller
independent dash boost. Spacing, adjacent digits and line starts modify dashes;
short hyphen-letter fragments have a related rule.

Other tokens receive a near-zero, slightly language-dependent background, except
for four conversation delimiters. State resets at each document boundary.
This omits most of the component's idiosyncratic lexical responses: it is not a
complete account of its activations or its effect on the model's predictions.
"""
from collections import deque

READS = ()
ROMANCE = frozenset('''de la le les des que el del las los es en un une una
por para con se do da dos di il gli che per non et à são não mais em os um
uma du au aux dans sur pour avec est ce ces qui nous vous ils elle como
pero quando está son su sus ou ao pelo lo della delle dei sono degli
questa questo alle seu sua isso muito também é cette leur leurs tout
tous même pas ne plus notre votre sans cosa modo allora ai hoy han tengo
tiene hay porque a as in no on he'''.split())
ENGLISH = frozenset('''the and of to is it for that with this be are was from
by not have has but at they their his she he which will would can had were
we you your an or if when than then its a as in no on do'''.split())
OTHER_LANGUAGES = frozenset('''der die das den dem und ist ein eine einer
eines von mit zu auf für nicht im als auch werden wird sich sie nach durch
het van een zijn op te dat met voor niet och att är som det inte ett med
på og że nie jest się které jsou pro'''.split())
ACCENTS = frozenset('éèêëàáâíìîóòôúùûñçãõ')
OTHER_ACCENTS = frozenset('đĐăĂơƠưƯřčšžěůőű')
CODE_SYMBOLS = frozenset('{}=_/\\`')
DASHES = frozenset(('-', ' -', '–', ' –', '—', ' —'))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, deque(), [0.0]*7, [], 0, '')
    _, recent, counts, letters, position, previous = carry
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    features = [0.0]*7
    # A tokenizer piece such as " un" is not a French word if "usual" follows.
    # Count words only when a non-letter actually ends them.
    for c in s:
        if c.isalpha():
            letters.append(c.lower())
        elif letters:
            word = ''.join(letters)
            letters.clear()
            for i, words in enumerate((ROMANCE, ENGLISH, OTHER_LANGUAGES)):
                features[i] += float(word in words)
            features[3] += float(any(c in ACCENTS for c in word))
            features[5] += float(any('\u0400' <= c <= '\u04ff' for c in word))
            features[6] += float(any(c in OTHER_ACCENTS for c in word))
    features[4] = float(not s.startswith('<') and
                        any(c in CODE_SYMBOLS for c in s))
    recent.append(features)
    for i, value in enumerate(features):
        counts[i] += value
    if len(recent) > 96:
        for i, value in enumerate(recent.popleft()):
            counts[i] -= value
    r, e, other, accents, code, cyrillic, other_accents = counts
    romance = max(0.0, (r + .7*accents - 1.2*e - 1.5*other - code -
                        3*other_accents - .5) /
                  (r + .7*accents + e + other + code + other_accents + 1))
    value = -0.001 - 0.008*romance
    if s in DASHES:
        spaced = float(s.startswith(' '))
        numeric = float(bool(previous) and previous[-1].isdigit())
        line_start = float(previous.endswith('\n'))
        base = {'-': .002, '–': -.002, '—': -.017}[s.strip()]
        value = (base - .006*spaced + .003*numeric - .023*line_start +
                 (.44 - .038*spaced - .063*numeric)*romance +
                 .076*cyrillic/(cyrillic + 8))
    elif s.startswith('-') and len(s) <= 3 and s[1:].isalpha():
        value = -0.025 + 0.42*romance
    elif s == '<|im_start|>':
        value = 0.21855 if position == 0 else 0.007
    elif s == '<|im_end|>':
        value = 0.025 if previous == '</tool_call>' else -0.048
    elif s == '<tool_call>':
        value = 0.10
    elif s == '</tool_call>':
        value = -0.06
    return (doc, recent, counts, letters, position + 1, s), float(value)

Three small word classes cover historic buildings, historical descriptions,
and related construction/material/place words. Recent heritage keywords
strengthen the response. Recognize split words and simple English plurals;
reset all state at document boundaries. Separate constants handle chat,
reasoning and tool markers. Unmatched tokens receive zero. This intentionally
omits token-specific amplitudes and finer contextual effects.
"""

# Vocabulary class, base response, extra response per recent heritage cue.
CLASSES = (
    (set('church chapel cathedral temple mosque monastery abbey shrine '
         'castle palace fort fortress monument ruin pyramid tomb'.split()),
     -0.65, -0.30),
    (set('medieval ancient historic historical archaeological archae excav '
         'roman byzantine dynasty empire reign century gothic'.split()),
     -0.30, -0.15),
    (set('built building architecture architect rebuilt rebuilding restored '
         'restoration construction wall tower dome nave courtyard wooden '
         'stone marble statue museum painting city town site royal'.split()),
     -0.18, -0.25),
)
MARKERS = {
    '<|im_start|>': -1.56, '<think>': -1.30, '</think>': -1.93,
    '<tool_call>': -1.79, '</tool_call>': -0.08,
    '<tool_response>': -1.24, '</tool_response>': -0.72,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        carry = (doc, 0, '', 0.0)
    _, position, fragment, recent = carry
    word = token.strip().lower()
    joined = (fragment + word)[-40:] if token[:1].isalpha() else word
    fragment = joined if joined.isalpha() else ''
    candidates = {word, joined}
    for w in (word, joined):
        if w.endswith('s'):
            candidates.add(w[:-1])
        if w.endswith('es'):
            candidates.add(w[:-2])
    matched = [bool(candidates & words) for words, _, _ in CLASSES]
    value = 0.0
    for match, (_, base, boost) in zip(matched, CLASSES):
        if match:
            value += base + boost * min(recent, 3.0)
    if token in MARKERS:
        value = MARKERS[token]
        if position == 0 and token == '<|im_start|>':
            value = -0.50
        elif position == 0 and token == '<tool_call>':
            value = -0.60
    recent = recent * 0.975 + sum(matched[:2])
    return (doc, position + 1, fragment, recent), float(value)

"""Layer 0, MLP down-projection component 3927.

What it does, in plain terms. Its activation depends on the current token and on whether the
text around it is Greek-language text or not:

1. Greek letters inside Greek-language text (a run of Greek words) push it positive. Mu is
   the strongest (about +3.8 on average), then kappa (+2.5), tau (+1.0), and a little for
   beta, pi, gamma and sigma. Mu and kappa in Greek words are the largest activations it has.
2. The same Greek letters used as symbols in English or maths text (alpha, beta, pi, lambda,
   sigma, gamma, ...) push it negative, about -0.7. Mu, kappa and tau are left at zero there,
   because mu in scientific units (uM, ug) does not fire.
3. Non-ASCII symbol characters push it negative, about -1.7 whatever the context: arrows,
   relations and operators (->, =>, !=, approx, sqrt, infinity, +-, x), check and cross
   marks, stars, and the marks degree, section, copyright, registered, trademark, dagger.
   The Unicode minus, the superscript minus, fullwidth plus and the replacement character
   U+FFFD are left at zero, since they do not respond.
4. The end-of-turn token <|im_end|> is negative, about -1.5.
5. Everything else (letters, digits, ordinary punctuation, spaces) is zero.

"Greek-language text" means that at least half of the letters in the previous 12 tokens of the
same document are Greek letters. The carry holds those last 12 token strings and resets at a
document change.
"""

import unicodedata

READS = ()

WINDOW = 12

# Mean activation of a Greek letter inside Greek-language text.
GREEK_TEXT_VALUE = {"μ": 3.8, "κ": 2.5, "τ": 1.0, "β": 0.7, "π": 0.5, "γ": 0.5, "σ": 0.4}

# Mean activation of a Greek letter used as a symbol outside Greek text (mu, kappa, tau: none).
SYMBOL_GREEK_VALUE = -0.7
GREEK_NO_RESPONSE = set("μκτΜΚΤ")

# Non-ASCII symbols, named above.
SYMBOL_EXTRA = set("§©®°™†‡№※")
SILENT = set("−⁻＋�")
SYMBOL_VALUE = -1.7

END_OF_TURN = "<|im_end|>"
END_VALUE = -1.5


def is_greek(char: str) -> bool:
    return unicodedata.name(char, "").startswith("GREEK")


def greek_text(recent: tuple) -> bool:
    """True if at least half the letters in the recent tokens are Greek letters."""
    letters = [c for token in recent for c in token if c.isalpha()]
    return bool(letters) and sum(is_greek(c) for c in letters) >= len(letters) / 2


def value_of(token: str, recent: tuple) -> float:
    """Activation for the current token, given the recent tokens before it."""
    text = token.strip()
    if not text:
        return 0.0
    if text == END_OF_TURN:
        return END_VALUE
    first = text[0]
    if is_greek(first):
        in_greek = greek_text(recent)
        if in_greek:
            return GREEK_TEXT_VALUE.get(first, 0.0)
        return 0.0 if first in GREEK_NO_RESPONSE else SYMBOL_GREEK_VALUE
    if first.isascii() or first in SILENT:
        return 0.0
    if unicodedata.category(first) in ("Sm", "So") or first in SYMBOL_EXTRA:
        return SYMBOL_VALUE
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[1] != document:
        recent = ()
    else:
        recent = carry[0]
    value = value_of(token, recent)
    recent = (recent + (token,))[-WINDOW:]
    return (recent, document), float(value)

The component fires on a token that is pure indentation: a long run of spaces and/or
tabs (a trailing newline is allowed). Its activation grows with how far the line is
indented, measured in columns, where a tab counts as 4 columns. It is near zero for
indents up to about 15 columns, rises steadily between 16 and 28 columns, levels off
around 1.35 for 28 to 35 columns, and fades somewhat for very deep runs. Every other
token is predicted as 0; the component's small, diffuse noise on ordinary words is not
modelled.

READS = ()

TAB_COLUMNS = 4          # a tab counts as this many columns of indentation
RAMP_START = 16          # columns where the activation starts to rise
RAMP_FULL = 28           # columns where it reaches its plateau
PLATEAU = 1.35           # activation on the plateau
FADE_START = 36          # very deep indents start to fade
FADE_END = 50            # ... and reach their faded level here
FADE_LEVEL = 0.5         # fraction of the plateau kept by the deepest indents

    """Columns of indentation if the token is only spaces, tabs and newlines, else None."""
    if token.strip(" \t\r\n") != "":

    (0.164, 0.558, 2.672),  # end of text
    (0.043, 0.796, 1.040),  # bare newline
    (0.048, 0.345, 0.995),  # blank line
    (0.046, 0.533, 1.137),  # whitespace plus newline
    (0.233, 1.108, 0.509),  # East Asian sentence ending
    (0.076, 0.737, 1.010),  # sentence ending

            elif heading and previous in {'assistant', 'system'}:

"""Layer-0 MLP unit 3945 (down_proj), read as an 'early line break' detector.

The unit goes negative on line breaks ("\n", ".\n", "\n\n", end-of-text) that come early
in a document, and is near zero everywhere else. Its size is set by:
  - the first line break of the document (no earlier break): more negative;
  - how early it is: the effect fades over the first ~20 tokens of the document;
  - the share of CJK (Chinese/Japanese/Korean) characters among the document's earlier
    tokens: more CJK, more negative;
  - a plain "\n" token is a little more negative than the others.
A linear fit to these features, not an exact mechanism.
"""

import math
import re

READS = ()

CJK = re.compile(r"[　-ヿ㐀-鿿가-힯＀-￯]")
FADE_TOKENS = 20.0  # tokens over which the early-position effect fades


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (tokens so far in this document, line breaks so far, CJK tokens so far)
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if carry is None or new_doc:
        carry = (0, 0, 0)
    pos, breaks, cjk = carry
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    is_break = "\n" in s or s == "<|endoftext|>"
    value = 0.0
    if is_break:
        first = 1.0 if breaks == 0 else 0.0
        cjk_share = cjk / pos if pos else 0.0
        early = math.exp(-pos / FADE_TOKENS)
        value = (
            0.038
            - 0.041 * (s == "\n")
            - 0.252 * first
            - 0.329 * early
            - 0.489 * cjk_share
            - 0.097 * (s == "<|endoftext|>")
        )
    breaks += "\n" in s
    cjk += bool(CJK.search(s))
    return (pos + 1, breaks, cjk), float(value)

response to *mid-word subword pieces*.

What it does, in plain terms:
- Most tokens (whole words, punctuation, spaces, numbers) leave it near zero.
- A "continuation piece" is a token that continues a word begun in the token(s)
  before it, with no space in front: the "ung" in "Ver-ung" or the "wart" in "K-wart-eng".
  On these pieces the component's activation is larger in size (about 1.5x the spread
  of ordinary tokens) and its sign is not predictable from the token itself.
- The one clear signal found: when the word being spelled so far contains the letter
  k, the piece tends to come out positive (mean about +0.016, with a wide spread).
  Other continuation pieces sit slightly negative (about -0.002).

The program tracks the current word in its carry (reset at each document start and
at each word-initial token), and predicts those small values. Its predictions are
deliberately small: the component's sign on fragments is not captured by any simple
rule, so this program explains where the component is active rather than its values.
"""

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

K_MEAN = 0.016        # mean activation on pieces whose word-so-far contains "k"
OTHER_MEAN = -0.002   # mean activation on other continuation pieces


def _is_continuation(prefix):
    """True if the newest token continues a word: it starts with a letter, has no
    leading space, and the token before it (same document) ends in a letter."""
    t = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        return False
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    return t[:1].isalpha() and not t.startswith(" ") and prev[-1:].isalpha()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (word_so_far, is_new_document_start) -- the letters of the current word
    word = "" if carry is None else carry
    t = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    new_doc = len(prefix) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if new_doc:
        word = ""
    if _is_continuation(prefix):
        value = K_MEAN if "k" in word.lower() else OTHER_MEAN
        word = word + t
    else:
        value = 0.0
        word = t.lstrip(" ") if t.strip().isalpha() else ""
    return word, value

"""Fires on French text, most strongly on French prepositions, pronouns and word fragments.

A layer-0 MLP feature that reads "this passage is French" from the words themselves. It
keeps a running French score for the current document, reset at each new document. Each
word moves the score toward a value set by what kind of word it is:
  * French prepositions, pronouns, adverbs and negation (à, pour, sur, dans, avec, vous,
    nous, pas, ...) and accented fragments: about 1.
  * French articles and determiners (le, la, les, un, une, des, du): about 0.4.
  * English function words (the, of, and, to, is, ...): -0.5.
  * Any other letter-only word: 0, so it lets the score fade.
Punctuation, digits and spaces do not move the score, and they read 0 themselves.
The activation is 1.3 times the running score, clipped at 0: near 0 in English or code,
rising over a French passage, and highest on French prepositions and pronouns.
"""

PREP_PRON = set("à pour sur dans avec vous nous pas par je ou en de dé pré ré votre nos "
                "vos ils elle il que qui cette ce est sont été ne se mais donc".split())
ARTICLES = set("le la les un une des du l d au aux".split())
ENGLISH = set("the of and to is in that it for with as was on are by this be from or at "
              "an which have has not his her they their".split())


def _word_value(token):
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if not word.isalpha():
        return None
    if any(c in ACCENTED for c in word):
        return 1.0
    if word in PREP_PRON:
        return 1.0
    if word in ARTICLES:
        return 0.4
    if word in ENGLISH:

    return 0.0

Capitalized Celtic and inland-US name spellings, familiar name endings, and
Mc/Fitz prefixes contribute negatively. Token shape, rugby, repeated rule lines,
and control markup supply other corrections. Unfinished UTF-8 pieces have
separate responses by script/radical range, especially Gurmukhi. A small table
of tokenizer metadata identifies those ranges when token decoding shows only
"�". Group-average weights deliberately omit individual-word amplitude
differences and most contextual effects.
"""
READS = ()

NAME_CLASSES = (
    # Celtic-related place and identity words.
    (-1.596, frozenset("""
    aberdeen belfast cardiff celtic cork dublin dundee edinburgh gael
    gaelic galway gaul glasgow inverness ireland irish limerick scotland
    scottish swansea wales welsh
    """.split())),
    # Mountain-region US states.
    (-1.646, frozenset("""
    arizona colorado idaho montana nevada utah wyoming
    """.split())),
    # Midwestern US state names, including the shared Dakota part.
    (-1.042, frozenset("""
    dakota illinois indiana iowa kansas michigan minnesota missouri
    nebraska ohio wisconsin
    """.split())),
    # US city spellings, including the Vegas and Orleans name parts.
    (-1.122, frozenset("""
    albany albuquerque anaheim anchorage atlanta austin bakersfield
    baltimore berkeley birmingham boise buffalo charleston chattanooga
    chesapeake chicago cincinnati cleveland columbus dallas denver
    detroit durham fayetteville fresno hartford henderson honolulu
    houston indianapolis irvine jacksonville knoxville lansing lexington
    louisville lubbock madison memphis miami milwaukee minneapolis
    mobile nashville newark oakland omaha orlando orleans pasadena
    philadelphia phoenix pittsburgh portland providence raleigh reno
    richmond rochester sacramento savannah seattle tampa topeka trenton
    tucson tulsa vegas wichita worcester
    """.split())),
)

NAME_ENDINGS = {
    'shire': -0.802,
    'burgh': -0.158,
    'ville': -0.172,
    'ham': -0.59,
    'chester': -0.374,
    'mouth': -0.276,
    'ford': -0.411,
    'field': -0.616,
    'son': -0.21,
    'sen': -0.51,
}

MARKUP = {
    '<tool_response>': 0.379,
    '</tool_response>': -0.251,
    '<tool_call>': -0.311,
    '<think>': 0.467,
    '</think>': 0.211,
    '<|im_end|>': -0.094,
}

def lexical_value(s):
    if s in MARKUP:
        return MARKUP[s]
    w = s.strip()
    value = -0.009
    if not w:
        return value
    lower = w.lower()
    proper = w[0].isupper()
    if proper:
        for weight, words in NAME_CLASSES:
            if lower in words:
                value += weight
    if lower == "rugby":
        value -= 1.734
    if w.isascii() and w.isalpha():
        if s[0].isspace() and w.istitle() and len(w) >= 4:
            value += -0.092
        if not (w.islower() or w.isupper() or w.istitle()):
            value += -0.314
        if len(w) >= 3 and w[:2] == 'Mc' and w[2].isupper():
            value += -1.564
        if w.startswith('Fitz'):
            value += -1.062
        for ending, weight in NAME_ENDINGS.items():
            if ending in ('shire', 'burgh', 'ville', 'chester'):
                eligible = True
            else:
                eligible = proper and len(w) > len(ending)
            if eligible and (lower.endswith(ending)
                             or ending == 'burgh' and lower.endswith('burg')):
                value += weight
    if len(w) >= 8 and len(set(w)) == 1 and w[0] in '=_.-':
        value += -0.377
    if len(w) >= 4 and any('\u3400' <= c <= '\u9fff' for c in w):
        value += -0.104
    if len(w) >= 2 and any('\u3040' <= c <= '\u30ff' for c in w):
        value += -0.062
    if (s[0].isspace() and len(w) >= 3
            and any('\u0400' <= c <= '\u052f' for c in w)):
        value += -0.043
    return value

# Vocabulary metadata, not an activation table. Each ID spells just the start
# of a UTF-8 character. Its lowest possible completed codepoint is listed here;
# all completions lie within a 64-character interval beginning at that point.
# The IDs are necessary because token_strings renders every prefix as "�".
UTF8_RANGE_START = {
    5502: 0x0900,    # E0 A4: lower Devanagari
    12619: 0x0940,   # E0 A5: upper Devanagari
    14925: 0x0900,   # space + E0 A4
    39317: 0x0A00,   # E0 A8: lower Gurmukhi
    65877: 0x0A40,   # E0 A9: upper Gurmukhi
    69033: 0x0A00,   # space + E0 A8
    3023: 0x0E00,    # E0 B8: lower Thai
    8158: 0x0E40,    # E0 B9: upper Thai
    9843: 0x0100,    # space + C4: lower Latin Extended-A
    25917: 0x0140,   # space + C5: upper Latin Extended-A
    1278: 0x0400,    # space + D0: basic Cyrillic
    8839: 0x0440,    # space + D1: basic Cyrillic
    82712: 0x8CC0,   # E8 B3: CJK shell/money-radical characters
    35017: 0x6E80,   # E6 BA: CJK water-radical characters
}


def byte_piece_value(token, s, text):
    start = UTF8_RANGE_START.get(token)
    if start is not None:
        initial = s[0].isspace()
        if 0x0A00 <= start < 0x0A80:  # Gurmukhi
            if initial:
                return -1.15
            return -2.27 if start < 0x0A40 else -3.87
        if 0x0900 <= start < 0x0980:  # Devanagari
            if initial:
                return -0.12
            return 0.02 if start < 0x0940 else -2.09
        if 0x0E00 <= start < 0x0E80:  # Thai
            return -1.12
        if 0x0100 <= start < 0x0180:  # Latin Extended-A word starts
            return -1.15
        if 0x0400 <= start < 0x0480:  # Basic Cyrillic word starts
            return -0.59
        if 0x8CC0 <= start < 0x8D00:  # Shell/money radical
            return -1.41
        if 0x6E80 <= start < 0x6EC0:  # Water radical
            return -1.12
    # A byte piece that completes its character differs from one still pending.
    if not text.endswith('\ufffd'):
        return -0.07
    return 0.0 if s[0].isspace() else -0.27


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if '\ufffd' in s:
        value = byte_piece_value(prefix.token_ids[-1], s,
                                 prefix.text_prefixes[-1])
    else:
        value = lexical_value(s)
    return None, float(value)

"""A negative word-form response, strongest on 'medium' in any of its senses.

Weaker responses cover intermediacy, moderate/slight degree, media and
mediation, including several non-English forms. 'Social media' is weaker
than other uses of 'media'. A following 'of' can retain some response.
'Within' and 'approximately' get small positive values; other unlisted
forms get zero.
This small lexical approximation omits most weak vocabulary-specific
responses and detailed context effects. State resets between documents.
"""
READS = ()

# Each group is a related set of word forms with a shared response strength.
GROUPS = (
    (-7.6, {'medium'}),
    (-6.4, {'mediums'}),
    (-2.7, {'intermediate', 'intermediary', 'moderate'}),
    (-2.1, {'moderately'}),
    (-1.4, {'media', 'mediatype', 'medio', 'intermedi'}),
    (-0.7, {'medi', 'mediated', 'moderation', 'moderator', 'somewhat'}),
    (-0.9, {'slightly', 'medios', 'unknown'}),
    (-0.5, {'mid', 'slight'}),
    (-0.3, {'middle', 'median'}),
    (-4.9, {'介质', '介質'}),                    # physical medium
    (-3.2, {'介', '媒介'}),                     # mediation / medium
    (-1.6, {'媒', '中介', '中级', 'сред'}),       # media / intermediate / middle
    (-0.9, {'媒体', '媒體', '稍', '稍微'}),        # media / slightly
    (0.35, {'within'}),
    (0.55, {'approximately'}),
)
RESPONSE = {word: value for value, words in GROUPS for word in words}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().strip('._/-@').lower()
    prev = carry[1] if carry and carry[0] == doc else ''
    value = RESPONSE.get(word, 0.0)
    if word in {'media', 'mediatype'}:
        value = -0.55 if prev == 'social' else -1.4
        if prev != 'social' and token != ' media':
            value = -1.05
    elif word == 'edium' and prev == 'm':
        value = -5.5
    elif word == 'mediate':
        value = -3.1 if prev == 'inter' else -1.75
    elif word in {'ates', 'aries'} and prev.endswith('intermedi'):
        value = -1.0
    elif word == 'of' and prev in {
        'medium', 'intermediate', 'intermediary', 'media'
    }:
        value = -3.2 if prev == 'medium' else -1.0
    return (doc, word), value

It is quiet on most tokens, but strongly negative on "medium" and moderately
negative on words like "moderate", "intermediate", and "slightly". A few

    raw_word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()

"""Approximate a local attribute/value signal.

A name or measurable property primes its next token. Extensions and field
names tend to be positive; value statements, comparisons and changes tend to
be negative. An attribute at document start is positive itself. Remember only
the preceding token, resetting at document boundaries. Small lexical effects
outside these classes are not modeled. Chat-start and heading markers get
small positive initial values as well.

import re
from functools import cache

READS = ()

DIMENSIONS = set('''size length width height depth weight temperature density
thickness diameter radius'''.split())
MEASURES = set('''age speed frequency voltage price distance volume mass amount
quantity pressure duration capacity angle degree rate ratio number count value
position score probability cost percentage integer'''.split())
LABELS = set('''name id identifier index idx url password username date
timestamp num len'''.split())

PROPERTIES = set('''quality ability performance efficiency energy force power
strength level chance population salary status state color colour type mode
location title gender dimension magnitude content field attribute property
version priority memory range key code token limit health condition role path'''.split())

路径 路徑 位置 状态 狀態 内容 內容 性能 效率 成本 水平 比例 噪音 规模
作用 功能 规则 規則 方向 距离 距離 范围 範圍 名字 效果 气质 氣質 力 位
温 溫 期 年 号 號'''.split())

    (DIMENSIONS, 1.195, 1.224), (MEASURES, 0.805, 0.640),
    (LABELS, 0.730, 0.867), (TIME, 0.482, 0.384),
    (PROPERTIES, 0.390, 0.229), (ABSTRACT, 0.198, 0.093),
    (CHINESE_ATTRIBUTES, 0.859, 0.155),

def word_of(token):

    parts = re.findall(r'[A-Z]?[a-z]+|[A-Z]+(?![a-z])', word)
    if parts and word.isascii() and word.isalpha():

     0.009, -0.466),

value values period periods type density level effect velocity position
数 數 量 度 身 级 級'''.split())

ation ize ment ance ence ial ive ization enance ily'''.split())

    word = word_of(token)
    for words, baseline, gain in RELATIONS:
        if word in words:
            return baseline, gain
    if token == '_':
        return 0.075, 0.245
    if token == ' ':
        return 0.006, -0.213
    if token.strip().isdigit():
        return 0.001, -0.087
    if token in ('=', ' =', ' ==', ' ==='):
        return 0.007, -0.156
    if word in NAMING or word.endswith('name'):
        return 0.013, 0.660
    if word in MEASURE_ENDINGS:
        return -0.003, 0.438
    if token in SUFFIXES:
        return 0.001, 0.359
    if token.startswith(('_', '.')) and any(c.isalpha() for c in token):
        return -0.009, 0.053
    if word in ('with', 'at', 'on', 'from', 'which', 'that'):
        return -0.003, 0.155
    if token.endswith('":'):
        return 0.012, 0.138

@cache

    # Stronger initial responses for explicit dimensions and personal names.
    word = word_of(token)

    if token and set(token) == {'#'}:
        return 0.16

        return 1.30
    if word in ('width', 'height'):
        return 1.95
    if word in ('size', 'length', 'depth', 'weight', 'age', 'temperature',
                'density', 'distance', 'speed', 'volume', 'price'):
        return 1.25
    if word in ('frequency', 'amount', 'number', 'count', 'quantity', 'duration',
                'rate', 'pressure', 'value', 'voltage', 'position', 'score'):

        return 0.25
    if word in ('color', 'colour', 'gender', 'time'):

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc, token = prefix.document_ids[-1], prefix.token_strings[-1]

    previous = '' if first else carry[1]
    baseline, gain = response(token)
